item.title: Agricultural Stress Index near real time (Global - Dekadal - 1 km ) - FAO ASIS
item.description:
Agricultural Stress Index (ASI) is a quick-look indicator that facilitates the early identification of cropped land with a high likelihood of water stress (drought). It depicts the percentage of arable land, within an administrative area, that has been affected by drought conditions from the start of the season up to the current dekad. It differs from ASI Annual product which describes the drought conditions over the entire crop season.

Phenomenon Mapped: Agricultural Stress Index 

Units: Percent

Time Interval: 10-day

Time Extent: 1984-Present

Cell Size: 1 km

Pixel Type: 32-bit Signed Integer

Data Projection: WGS 1984

Mosaic Projection: WGS 1984 Web Mercator

Source: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

Update Cycle: 10-days + 3-4 days lag

 

The Index is based on the integration of the Vegetation Health Index (VHI) in two dimensions that are critical in the assessment of a drought event in agriculture: temporal and spatial. The first step of the ASI calculation is a temporal averaging of the VHI, assessing the intensity and duration of dry periods occurring during the crop cycle at the pixel level; this calculation includes the use of crop coefficients, which introduces sensitivity of a crop to water stress during each phenological phase. The second step determines the spatial extent of drought events by calculating the percentage of pixels in arable areas with a VHI value below 35 percent (this value was identified as a critical threshold in assessing the extent of drought in previous research by Kogan, 1995). Each administrative area is classified according to the percentage of the affected area to facilitate the quick interpretation of results.
 
This index is computed in two temporal granularities: Near Real Time (10 days) and Annual Summary. Historic Drought Frequency dataset is also computed based on the entire ASI Annual Summary datasets (1984-2024).
 
 
Explore this and related data in this web application.
 
More information please visit FAO GIEWS Earth Observation website
item.snippet:
Agricultural Stress Index System (ASIS) is a global agricultural drought monitoring system developed and operated by United Nations Food and Agricultural Organization (UN FAO). It combines the expert knowledge on remote sensing, agronomy, agrometeorology and land use with big earth data, simulates the behaviors of domain experts and simplifies the interpretation of remote sensing data for a broader audience. ASIS was online in 2014 and is updated by FAO GIEWS every dekad (10 days), around 2-3 days after a dekad ends.

ASIS is composed of two types of indicators: seasonal and no-seasonal indicators. Seasonal indictors include Agricultural Stress Index (ASI), Drought Intensity and Mean Vegetation Health Index. Two cropping cycles (season 1/season 2) and two types of land (cropland and grassland) are applied. The indicators are computed in two modalities: dekadal and annual.Agricultural Stress Index is a quick-look indicator that facilitates the early identification of cropped land with a high likelihood of water stress or drought. This layer updates every 10-days.
item.licenseInfo:
Data access: Apart from ESRI/ArcGIS platform, all ASIS raster datasets (global extent, 1 km resolution, 1984-present, over 16, 000 raster layer) can be accessed in various ways: FAO Hand-in-Hand Geospatial Portal (HiH GP), Google Earth Engine (GEE) platform and Image Services (WMS) provided by FAO.  ASIS pre-processed, published-ready products (static maps/graphs/time series zonal statistics), originated from the raster datasets, can be accessed at: FAO GIEWS Earth Observation website.
